title: Federated Nonlinear Causal Discovery via Divide-and-Conquer Learning

problem.claim: Federated causal discovery seeks to learn causal structures from distributed data without sharing raw samples.

gap.claim: Existing federated nonlinear methods use a monolithic global strategy that can suffer catastrophic error propagation under heterogeneous and limited local data.

contributions.claim: DC-FNCD decomposes federated nonlinear causal discovery into independent per-variable neighborhood learning tasks.
The method uses a characteristic function-based conditional independence test with empirical statistics that linearly decompose across clients for federated aggregation without raw data exchange.
The method merges local neighborhoods through conflict-aware skeleton construction and orients them using federated additive noise model testing.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show DC-FNCD significantly outperforms state-of-the-art federated baselines.
The authors report that source code is available.

narrative_sequence.summary: Federated causal discovery learns causal structures from distributed data without sharing raw samples.
Monolithic global federated nonlinear methods are vulnerable to cascading errors, especially with heterogeneous and limited local data.
DC-FNCD divides the global problem into independent per-variable neighborhood learning tasks.
Characteristic-function conditional independence testing enables lossless aggregation across clients, followed by conflict-aware neighborhood merging and federated additive noise model orientation.
Experiments reportedly show significant improvement over state-of-the-art federated baselines.

unknowns: Datasets, baseline identities, evaluation metrics, and quantitative experimental results are unspecified.
The assumptions and computational costs of the conditional independence tests and additive noise model testing are unspecified.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported performance.
